title: [CQ-R08] Scoped host guest bridge
description:
Objective: Use fixed-command bounded stdio framing for task-scoped agent requests and supervisor-only observations.

Deliverable: Scoped host guest bridge. This is task R08 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): R07, F06.
definitionOfDone: Guest cannot reach raw host /mcp or /ws.
Caller-controlled role/worker IDs cannot elevate capabilities or change settings/dependencies.
Child stdout cannot impersonate supervisor protocol frames.
Fresh verification `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

comments.author: architect-26ba32c3
comments.content:
Split on 2026-10-25 (architect-26ba32c3). The full bridge measured at about 650 net LOC: a host codec and scoping module, a guest supervisor in Python (the guest has python3 but no Node), a host session, and tests. That is far over the 400-net-LOC QA limit, and no rail waives it. Following this epic's M01 and C02 pattern, this row keeps its full DoD and becomes the final slice, depending on:
- CQ-R08a task-f981d059 (PLANNING): scripts/local-runner/guest-bridge.mjs, which is the frame protocol, guest frame schema, per-role request scoping and fixed bridgeArgv. Tests go in the new scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs, registered in CI.
- CQ-R08b task-502c00a5 (BACKLOG): scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py, a stdlib-only supervisor that is the sole writer of its stdout. It relays child output only as base64 output frames and reports exit only from its own waitpid.
- CQ-R08c task-10e201f9 (BACKLOG): the agent request ingress, a Unix socket that admits only the moe-agent peer uid, assigns its own ids, and routes each response back to the requester only.

What remains for this row, to plan once the three slices land:
- The host bridge session: run bridgeArgv through the R06 invoker style with an injected spawn, require hello first, pump frames, and pass each request through scopeRequest and an injected forward. Bound in-flight requests and time them out, deliver output and observations to callbacks, and fail closed by killing the child on any violation.
- A loopback-only daemon guard: refuse to open when `.moe/daemon.json` records a non-loopback bindHost. That is WSL agent mode's 0.0.0.0, which a Multipass guest could reach through its gateway.
- An end-to-end test between the JS session and the real Python supervisor that proves DoD 1-3.
Verification: `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs`. It is a superset of the DoD command, so local-runner.test.mjs, which R04 and R05 also edit, is never touched.

comments.author: worker-c1d9de02
comments.content:
Handoff from CQ-R08a (task-f981d0597b26401a974c0fcd8829107e, guest-bridge.mjs). This is a requirement for the CQ-R08 forwarding path, not a defect in R08a.

1. Deeply nested args. parseGuestFrame and scopeRequest enforce exact keys and allowlists but no nesting depth. A guest frame within 256 KiB can carry about 100k levels of nesting in an allowed arg value, and JSON.parse accepts it. Re-serializing such a value can throw RangeError (stack overflow). encodeFrame already catches that and returns BRIDGE_FRAME_INVALID, but the CQ-R08 forwarding must catch JSON.stringify/send errors too, or bound the depth before forwarding, so a guest cannot crash the host session or the daemon.
2. Duplicate JSON keys. JS JSON.parse keeps the last occurrence of a duplicate key, and Python json does too by default. The R08b/c supervisor should not rely on first-wins.
3. Lost frames on error. Any decoder error poisons it, and any frames already decoded in the same push are discarded. The session should treat a throw as teardown.

comments.author: qa-b0c1741e
comments.content: QA note from the CQ-R08a review, for planning CQ-R08. guest-bridge.mjs TOOLS (in 17bc7ac) matches every committed daemon inputSchema. However, the uncommitted CQ-F06 edit (task-b03c0c7744e84955a7a069255a124ef7, Served context identity) adds a `sessionId` property to the moe.get_context schema. Today a guest-sent sessionId gets BRIDGE_ARGUMENT_DENIED, which fails closed. Once F06 lands, CQ-R08 should decide explicitly between two options: stamp a host-owned sessionId from the binding (preferred, since a receipt binds to the owning attempt), or keep refusing it. It should not add sessionId to the guest argument allowlist without a decision. Also note the B9 pin in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs, which any table change must update.

comments.author: worker-7d158765
comments.content:
CQ-R08b (task-502c00a5) handoff: two gaps in the guest-supervisor relay that belong downstream, not in R08b.
1. A silent child and a host that has gone: the relay notices only on its next frame write (EPIPE → exit 74, then killpg+reap). CQ-R08c should put stdin (host frames) in the same selectors loop, so host EOF ends the session promptly.
2. A SIGTERM or SIGHUP sent to the supervisor uses the default action and kills Python without running the finally. The child's session group (start_new_session) then survives. Only KeyboardInterrupt/OSError paths kill and reap today. Signal-driven teardown belongs to CQ-R08 or CQ-R10/R11.
Exit-code contract for the host session: 0 relay complete; 64 usage; 71 child failed to start (hello, then EOF, no observation); 74 I/O failure (child group killed); 77 not root; 78 root with no job. relay also resets SIGCHLD to SIG_DFL, because an inherited SIG_IGN would let the kernel discard the status before waitpid reads it.
